verdict: The engineering behind Own Hub's privacy promise is real and unusually careful. Images are never written. The NID is kept only as a peppered HMAC. Health data needs consent and the rules enforce it. Consent records cannot be edited. Deletion has a manifest and resweeps, and the site has a strict CSP with no scripts. Fixes should build on these parts and leave them as they are. The gaps are mostly about trust she cannot see or record. The legal links are empty and the site has placeholders. The C06 agreement has no record and no US notice. Crashlytics turns on before consent and has no toggle. There is no export. The AI promise is true but never stated. And a few public claims (video-call reviewer, no microphone, 'deleted' vs 'never stored') run ahead of the build. Each gap can be closed without slowing the value-first flow, by reusing the C09b consent pattern and the deletion manifest.

verdict: This cannot ship to either store as it stands, and it is legally exposed in Egypt. The engineering is strong. Tests are green, the camera-consent gate is solid, health data stays on the phone and the server logs are clean. What fails is consent and disclosure. Her phone number reaches the US before any consent while the policy claims the opposite, and no Terms or Privacy acceptance is recorded (S1). Crashlytics runs from first launch with no off switch (S4). The biometric consent text understates what is kept (S5). No policy link exists in the app (S2), and the public pages carry 11 placeholders per language plus drafting notes (S3). The reviewer video call is promised but has no vendor (S6). The privacy labels on both stores under-declare (S8, S9), there is no App Review path (S10), no in-app medical disclaimer (S11) and no export (S7). The code fixes (S1, S4, S5, S8, S9, S11, S15) are small and can be done this week. The real deadline is owner-side: the PDPC filing before 31 Oct, counsel sign-off, the video vendor, a real domain and a role mailbox (S2, S3, S6, S17). Assumptions the code makes about customers, which only real users can confirm: (1) she will hand her national ID and a live selfie to an app before seeing any value, now softened by the O03 and O05 value-first flow; (2) the check takes about 90 seconds; (3) a 72-hour reviewer SLA is acceptable for niqab-wearing women and those who fail three times; (4) she is 18 or over and holds an Egyptian NID, with no route for foreign residents; (5) she accepts that her number is handled in the US and her data in Frankfurt; (6) she will read MSA Arabic comfortably; (7) a free app with no export, community or coaching keeps her past day one; (8) she trusts a deletion process that ends in a phone call from the publisher; (9) she wants cycle and health data on the phone only, with backup off by default; (10) camera-only capture with no gallery upload works on the phones she owns.

approach:
I did not receive separate Skeptic findings, so I scored each open or partial checklist gap as a finding. Each has an impact score from 1 to 5 (risk of store rejection, a PDPL fine or prison, or a lawsuit, weighed against what it costs if it happens), an effort (S, M or L) and a confidence (Evidence or Assumption). I re-checked the most important facts in the uncommitted worktree. In legal_links.dart (lines 18-28) all four URLs are still empty. In firebase_boot.dart (lines 149-153) Crashlytics turns on in release at boot, and the native default is off (Info.plist lines 72-73). your_data_sheet.dart (lines 26-28) confirms there is no export. My search tool did not work in this environment (ripgrep missing), so placeholder counts, the missing acceptance record and the AR site parity come from the checklist's same-day re-check, not my own. I treated those as Evidence from the checklist, not from me. I have no Advocate PROTECTS CORE list. So I kept the core intact by default: the value-first order (O03 and O05 before the phone screen), C09b sensitive consent kept separate, health data on the phone only, and images never stored. No fix below touches any of these. I never estimate market or customer behaviour. Anything about users is marked as an assumption.

SECTION 1. IF WE ONLY FIX THREE THINGS.
(1) Hire an Egyptian lawyer now and file with the PDPC (LAW-01, LAW-17, APL-01, LAW-06). The grace period ends 31 Oct or 1 Nov, 25 days away, and Art. 41 and 42 penalties reach EGP 5M and/or prison for sensitive and cross-border data, which this app processes on day one. The same lawyer's answers fill every placeholder in privacy and terms and decide individual versus company. That decision gates the store accounts, so one engagement unblocks about 15 items.
(2) Build "Agree and continue" on C06 with a server-side acceptance record, and gate Crashlytics on it (OWN-03, OWN-04, LAW-03). Today her phone number goes to Firebase Auth in the US and crash data leaves the phone before any consent, which breaks PDPL Art. 14-16 and contradicts the policy. One change of about a day closes three legal items and gives us click-wrap evidence for every later dispute.
(3) Build a reviewer demo path: an Auth test number plus one pre-seeded verified uid (APL-03). No Apple or Google reviewer can pass Egyptian phone OTP plus a national ID plus a selfie, so without it rejection is certain on both stores, every time. It costs about half a day and removes the single most predictable rejection.

SECTION 2. FIX PLAN: see findings F1 to F10, ordered by impact, then by lowest effort. Each one says how we will know it worked.

SECTION 3. NOT WORTH FIXING NOW: see the keep list and the verdict.

SECTION 4. OUT OF CODE: the owner_action findings, each with one cheap real-world test.

verdict: This build should not be submitted, and it should not launch in Egypt yet. As the App Reviewer, I would reject it on both stores for four reasons. First, 2.1 and Play App access: there is no reviewer path past OTP, the Egyptian ID and a selfie. Second, 5.1.1(i): no privacy policy is reachable in the app, and all four LegalLinks are empty. Third, 5.1.1 and 5.1.2 and Play User Data: the privacy manifest leaves out SensitiveInfo, PhotosorVideos and ML Kit performance data, and Data safety leaves out Name and the age and sex taken from the ID. Fourth, 1.4.1 and Google Health: there is no 'not a medical device' line in the app. The public pages also still show draft banners and 22 placeholders, 11 in English and 11 in Arabic. The Arabic ones use a marker the checklist's grep does not catch. As the Plaintiff Lawyer, my strongest claims are: 1. The Terms and Privacy are never accepted or recorded, so the injury and liability limits fail. 2. The phone number goes to the US before any consent, while the privacy policy says consent comes first. 3. The C09b biometric consent says nothing is kept except the hash, which is false, and its wording changed without a version bump. 4. Crashlytics turns on at first launch with no consent and no off switch. 5. Workout and meal sync to Germany, including the Ramadan setting (a religious signal), has no transfer consent. 6. The woman-reviewer, 'no man ever sees' and support-hours claims do not match operations. 7. Fraud-signal records are kept forever and are not disclosed. 8. No PDPC permit, no legal entity and no breach runbook, 25 days before the deadline. 9. The women-only and ID requirement is hard to justify as proportionate while the launch build connects her to no one. The camera-consent gate, NID-only sex reading, image non-retention, health-backup consent, deletion engine and permissions are solid and should be kept. Priority order: C06 click-wrap and US disclosure with a recorded acceptance; corrected and version-bumped C09b text; consent-gated Crashlytics; complete the manifest and Data safety; fill and publish the legal pages with LegalLinks set; a reviewer test account; the in-app medical disclaimer; then the counsel memo, PDPC filing and entity decision.
